answer: Practically, the chain should attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because gale only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, juniper is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any signal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
